A subset of assembly instructions can be inserted into C code by using VS compiler intrinsics
These look like C functions calls, but the compiler substitutes them with literal assembly instructions
Visual Studio supports inline assembler for 32-bit code, but not x86-64
Hand-written assembly must be written in MASM (Microsoft Assembler syntax) in a separate .asm file, with exported function names, and then called from your C code and linked to by the linker
How to create a basic project is shown on the site, but one has been provided already in the "scratchpad_asm" project

Writing instructions via raw bytes can be used to test your understanding of instruction encoding as specified in the manual
Also sometimes useful if you can't find the correct syntax for the specific assembler you're using, but you know exactly what instruction you want
Just put it into scratchpad_asm, run it in the debugger, and then confirm what you expect happens after you step past the instruction
MASM doesn't like immediates that start with an alphabet character. They must be preceded by a zero
"mov rax, E09966C1A977E177h" yields a compile error
This also applies to raw bytes
